searchText: How to calculate an EIP-1559 transaction refund? If there is any refund though 😅 EIP-1559 doesn't change gas refund code. There is another EIP in London that does though (I don't remember the number). Ah ok Asking this because I've noticed that the following miner tip calculation formula does not work with EIP-1559 transactions, only with legacy ones: ```go effectiveTip := st.gasPrice if st.evm.ChainConfig().IsLondon(st.evm.Context.BlockNumber) { effectiveTip = cmath.BigMin(st.gasTipCap, new(big.Int).Sub(st.gasFeeCap, st.evm.Context.BaseFee)) } st.state.AddBalance(st.evm.Context.Coinbase, new(big.Int).Mul(new(big.Int).SetUint64(st.gasUsed()), effectiveTip)) ``` That's from geth source code <@!301186049323958275> Why it is not working for EIP-1559 transactions? Is there something else that affects the miner tip? I'm not familiar with Geth's implementation. Let me rewrite that with python pseudocode The EIP has python actual code if you want to just check that out. <@!301186049323958275> here ```py effective_tip = tx.gas_price if is_london(block.number): effective_tip = min(tx.gas_price, (tx.gas_price - block.base_fee_per_gas)) tip = receipt.gas_used * effective_tip ``` Did not find any mention on how the tip is distributed to the miner So this formula works for legacy transactions only What is the formula for EIP-1559 transactions? See this line in the EIP: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1559 ```py self.account(block.author).balance += gas_used * priority_fee_per_gas ``` Ah, `block.author` instead of `block.coinbase` 😅 `coinbase` is what I was Ctrl+F'ing haha I have no idea why people call it coinbase. in solidity it's `block.coinbase` This is how it is called in bitcoin 😄 In Geth it is also block.Coinbase OE calls it `author` I think it should be standardized 😄 `block.validator` That could also work But it may confuse people Since there are no "validators" on eth1 chain I guess that `block.author` is indeed the best agree. Okay so using a "managed" `tx.EffectiveGasTip()` seems to fix that 😅 The yellow paper describes it as "beneficiary address". The EVM opcode to retrieve it is called COINBASE. The new executable eth1.0specs call it "coinbase", but they are very alpha. Question: How to get `gasTipCap` from `eth_getTransactionByHash` response? Or wait, is it the same `priorityFeeCap`? Get it from the receipt. Can't find it. There is only `effectiveGasPrice` `premium = effectiveGasPrice - block.baseFee` Ohhh makes sense Thank you <@!301186049323958275>

Asking this because I've noticed that the following miner tip calculation formula does not work with EIP-1559 transactions, only with legacy ones:
```go
effectiveTip := st.gasPrice
if st.evm.ChainConfig().IsLondon(st.evm.Context.BlockNumber) {
  effectiveTip = cmath.BigMin(st.gasTipCap, new(big.Int).Sub(st.gasFeeCap, st.evm.Context.BaseFee))
}
st.state.AddBalance(st.evm.Context.Coinbase, new(big.Int).Mul(new(big.Int).SetUint64(st.gasUsed()), effectiveTip))
```

```py
effective_tip = tx.gas_price
if is_london(block.number):
  effective_tip = min(tx.gas_price, (tx.gas_price - block.base_fee_per_gas))
tip = receipt.gas_used * effective_tip
```
